correctness.rationale: For normal T=A+iB, A and B commute and continuous functional calculus reduces the hypothesis exactly to abs(z) <= abs(Re z)+epsilon on the spectrum. With r=abs(z)<=M, the cases r>=epsilon and r<=epsilon give respectively abs(Im z)^2 <= 2 r epsilon-epsilon squared <= 2 M epsilon-epsilon squared and abs(Im z)^2 <= epsilon squared <= 2 M epsilon-epsilon squared. For epsilon>=M, norm(B)<=M. The displayed scalar choices attain both branches, including endpoints. No finite experiment is needed.

final_claim: For every bounded normal operator T with M = norm(T) satisfying abs(T) <= abs(Re T)+epsilon I, the optimal bound is norm(Im T) <= sqrt(2 M epsilon - epsilon squared) for zero <= epsilon <= M and norm(Im T) <= M for epsilon >= M; scalar operators attain equality for every parameter, so the sharp small-defect exponent in the normal class is one half.
